Subject: Baseline uptime + monthly stipend mechanics (proposal)

Hi Arya —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Based on Tempest's procurement ask (simpler monthly reconciliation, predictable cost modeling for runbooks) I've sketched an alternative to the incident-based credit approach: a small monthly "stipend" that Tier-1 customers can apply against service remedies rather than per-incident credits.

High-level summary (attached: SLA-stipend-matrix-v1.xlsx and redwood-sla-draft.docx):

- Baseline uptime: 99.95% per month across hosted endpoints (standard).
- Stipend pool: a monthly fixed stipend equal to 1.0% of monthly invoice, payable as a credit on the following invoice.
- When monthly uptime >= 99.95%: no stipend applied.
- When monthly uptime 99.80%–99.95%: stipend covers up to 50% of the calculated remedy.
- When monthly uptime < 99.80%: stipend applies first; additional remedial credits calculated pro rata by minutes below threshold.
- Latency SLO: P95 inference latency target by model/route (we include a per-route latency appendix). If latency SLOs miss we trigger a root-cause review but do not automatically escalate stipend amounts (we propose a separate remediation path).

Why this model? Procurement asked for: predictable monthly reconciliation, a capped liability, and faster settlement. The stipend gives Tempest predictable budget for reimbursement and reduces lengthy back-and-forth on small incidents. For Redwood, it caps exposure and simplifies bookkeeping versus ad-hoc credit calculations.

Ask: can you confirm whether a stipend-sized credit that posts automatically (rather than waiting for a claim) would satisfy your internal finance/legal teams? If so, we can prepare a tracked redline of the SLA with stipend mechanics and a short Annex clarifying measurement methodology.

If you'd like, I can loop in our legal lead (Ben Carter) and contracts counsel to accelerate a short-form amendment.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Growth, Redwood Inference

From: Arya Shah <arya@tempestlabs.com>

Cc: Tempest Labs Legal <legal@tempestlabs.com>
Date: Sun, 03 Aug 2025 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Baseline uptime + monthly stipend mechanics (proposal)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear write-up. High level: Finance likes the predictability; Legal wants clarity on measurement and a maximum payout cap for a single month. A few quick Qs from our end:

1) Measurement window: is the stipend calculation based on calendar month aligned to our billing cycle or UTC rolling 30 days? We prefer calendar month tied to invoice.
2) Cap: is the stipend additive to existing remedies or intended to replace small-incident credits? We want to ensure there is not double recovery.
3) Latency: can you add an example appendix showing how P95 latency across three high-volume routes maps to remediation steps?

From Legal (copied): "We need a clause that makes the stipend the exclusive remedy for incidents below $5k per month OR an explicit carve-out so larger incidents can still claim additional credits after stipend application."

If you can update the draft and share a tracked change version, we can review with procurement this week.

Cheers,
Arya Shah
Head of Platform Ops, Tempest Labs
arya@tempestlabs.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Baseline uptime + monthly stipend mechanics (proposal)

Ben / Laura —

Forwarding Tempest's reply. They want: calendar-month measurement, a max payout/cap language, and a P95 appendix for latency. Legal specifically asked about exclusivity vs. carve-outs for larger incidents.

Key constraints I recommend we consider: keep stipend as "first-dollar" automatic credit (posts with next invoice) but allow customers to pursue additional remedies for incidents above a materiality threshold (e.g., $5k) with a short claims process. That satisfies their ask for predictability while protecting Redwood when real outages occur.

Proposed edits I've highlighted in the attached redwood-sla-draft.docx:
- Section 3.1: define "measurement month" as calendar month aligned with billing.
- Section 4.2: stipend posted automatically as a credit = min(1% * monthly invoice, stipend cap).
- Section 4.3: exclusivity carve: stipend is exclusive remedy for monthly remediations up to $5k; above $5k customer can submit claim within 30 days with supporting telemetry.

Ben — can you take a pass on the legal language and suggest exact cap wording? Laura — any commercial objections to the $5k threshold or to making the stipend 1.0%?

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa —

Thanks for the ping and for drafting. I like the approach; it's a pragmatic compromise. A few redline suggestions (summary):

1) Cap mechanics: define a "monthly stipend cap" as the lesser of (a) 2.0% of the monthly invoice or (b) $25,000, whichever is lower. That gives a hard ceiling we can stand behind.

2) Exclusivity: good to have exclusivity for small amounts, but make the threshold tied to the monthly invoice instead of a fixed $5k: propose "exclusive remedy up to the greater of $5,000 or 0.5% of the monthly invoice." This scales with larger customers.

3) Measurement: agree to calendar-month aligned with billing. Include tie-breaker rules if invoice is prorated.

4) Latency appendix: we should explicitly exclude transient latency blips caused by customer-side throttling or malformed requests; we will include an examples table showing remediation steps and expected timeline.

I'll prepare a tracked word doc and push suggested edits to the redwood-sla-draft.docx. Laura — if commercial is comfortable with the cap ranges above, I'll send final draft for signature.
